newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Vale to be sold off April 18 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Vale to be sold off April 18 - paper.

text.p: The Brazilian government has set April 18 as the tentative auction date for the block sale of 40-45 percent of the voting shares of state mining conglomerate Vale do Rio Doce, O Estado de Sao Paulo reported Wednesday.

O Estado columnist Sonia Racy quoted an unnamed government source as saying officials had also privately set a $10 billion price tag for Vale, an amount which would be beneath the company's listed value.
The O Estado information could not be independently confirmed.
O Estado quoted the source as saying the government would only publicly announce a "definite" price for Vale two weeks before the final auction date.

The O Estado source said the final price would be determined by National Development Bank President Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros, Mines and Industry Minister Raimundo Britto and President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
Earlier this month government officials said the Vale tender details would be published at the end of February or early March and the block sale would "probably" take place 45 days after that.

The Brazilian government hopes to raise more than $5.0 billion by privatizing its 51 percent stake in Vale's total capital, first through the block sale and then via sales to staff and sales on international stock markets.
